content: 1. Tai et al. (2014) investigated the safety, tolerability, and adherence of a regimen combining raltegravir, emtricitabine, and tenofovir as post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) for HIV in men who have sex with men (MSM). The study was published in HIV Medicine. 2. Tan et al. (2014) explored the selection of antiretroviral regimens for occupational HIV post-exposure prophylaxis, focusing on the clinical considerations in healthcare settings. This research appeared in Infection Control and Hospital Epidemiology. 3. Bogoch et al. (2015) examined changes in initial PEP regimens between emergency departments and follow-up clinics, highlighting the practical challenges in maintaining consistent care. The findings were published in Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes. 4. Leal et al. (2016) conducted a randomized clinical trial comparing ritonavir-boosted lopinavir with raltegravir, both combined with tenofovir and emtricitabine, for HIV PEP. The results were published in Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy. 5. Fätkenheuer et al. (2016) performed a randomized, prospective, non-inferiority study (PEPDar) evaluating ritonavir-boosted darunavir for HIV PEP. The study was published in HIV Medicine. 6. Leal et al. (2016) also compared ritonavir-boosted lopinavir with maraviroc, each combined with tenofovir and emtricitabine, in a randomized clinical trial for HIV PEP. The findings were published in Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy. 7. Wiboonchutikul et al. (2016) reported significant intolerability of efavirenz in occupational HIV PEP regimens, emphasizing the need for alternative options. This study was published in Journal of Hospital Infection. 8. Milinkovic et al. (2017) conducted the MiPEP trial, a randomized controlled study comparing the tolerability and completion rates of maraviroc versus Kaletra® (lopinavir/ritonavir) in combination with Truvada® for HIV PEP. The results were published in Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy. 9. Inciarte et al. (2017) evaluated the use of tenofovir disoproxil fumarate/emtricitabine combined with either ritonavir-boosted lopinavir or cobicistat-boosted elvitegravir as a single-tablet regimen for HIV PEP. The study was published in Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy. 10. McAllister et al. (2017) assessed the efficacy of dolutegravir combined with tenofovir disoproxil fumarate/emtricitabine as HIV PEP in gay and bisexual men. The findings were published in AIDS. 11. Mayer et al. (2017) compared the completion rates of single-tablet daily regimens of elvitegravir/cobicistat/tenofovir disoproxil fumarate/emtricitabine with more frequent dosing regimens for optimal HIV PEP. The study was published in Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes. 12. Landovitz et al. (2015) demonstrated that contingency management strategies facilitated the use of PEP among stimulant-using MSM, addressing barriers to adherence. The study was published in Open Forum Infectious Diseases. 13. Fätkenheuer et al. (2014) presented the PEPDar study, a randomized trial comparing darunavir/ritonavir-based PEP with the standard of care, at the Conference on Retroviruses and Opportunistic Infections (CROI) in Boston, Massachusetts.
